title: 1inch Adds Four Stock-Linked Tokens on Base, Including Microsoft and AMD
description: The November expansion adds tokens linked to Microsoft, AMD, Sony and Take-Two to 1inch's Base offering, with swaps accessible through its app and wallet.
why_it_matters: The addition broadens the range of equity-linked assets available through a decentralized swap interface, but around-the-clock access does not establish share ownership rights, uniform liquidity or eligibility in every jurisdiction.
keyTakeaways: Four stock-linked tokens associated with Microsoft, AMD, Sony and Take-Two were added to the Base offering.
TokenPost says the instruments are accessible via the 1inch decentralized application or wallet.
The reported around-the-clock availability does not establish liquidity or the holder's legal rights.
body:
1inch has expanded the selection of stock-linked tokens accessible on Base, adding instruments associated with Microsoft, Advanced Micro Devices, Sony and Take-Two Interactive. TokenPost reported the four additions on November 14, while Coinfomania separately described the new batch and linked to a November announcement by the 1inch account. The tokens are presented as available through the 1inch decentralized application and wallet, rather than through a conventional stock brokerage interface.

The reports describe trading access around the clock, a feature that differs from the regular session of traditional equity exchanges. The expansion should not be confused with the initial introduction of stock-linked tokens to Base: it adds names to an existing offering. Neither report establishes trading volume, consistent liquidity, universal geographic availability or the legal rights conveyed by each token. Those details require issuer-specific documentation before users can equate the instruments with directly held shares.

facts.claim: TokenPost reports that 1inch brought four stock-linked tokens onto Base in its November expansion.
The four associated companies include Microsoft, Sony, Take-Two Interactive and Advanced Micro Devices.
TokenPost states that users can access these instruments through the decentralized application or wallet.
Coinfomania describes the new batch as accessible to traders around the clock.
